body.statement: For every sufficiently small \(h\) and every integer \(m\le c h^{\alpha\beta-d}\), there are disjoint cells \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) and a finite Gaussian subexperiment contained in \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\) whose alternatives change only one arm on \(\bigcup_{j=1}^mB_j\), have Hölder amplitude of order \(h^\beta\), satisfy the margin condition, and separate \(\theta(P)\) by order \(m h^{d+\beta}\) without sign cancellation. For every non-anticipating \(\mathsf D\), the trajectory divergence between neighboring alternatives is bounded above by \(C h^{2\beta}\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}N_a^{\mathsf D}(\bigcup_{j=1}^mB_j)\).
body.justification: The construction forces scalar targeting-gain separation, which ordinary label-flipping regret cubes can lose through cancellation.
body.gap: PerchetRigollet2013CovariateBandits supplies localized regret alternatives and HanJiaoMukherjee2020LrNorms supplies scalar-functional mixtures; neither proves membership and adaptive information control for the same family.
body.consumer: At \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), and \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\), this lemma is the early kill test for every proposed local-width exponent.
